title: Financial Conditions For The AI Capex Boom

Financial Conditions For The AI Capex Boom

Will Denyer, Tan Kai Xian

Gavekal Research | 25 Nov 2026

Semiconductor stocks and some data center operators have had a bruising five months as financial and political conditions for the artificial intelligence capital spending boom have worsened. Rising bond yields, persistent inflation, a hawkish Federal Reserve and a tougher political backdrop since the midterm elections have all weighed on sentiment, with the Jensen Huang affair compounding these pressures. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down -33% since October 5, while CoreWeave, Oracle and Alphabet have also fared poorly. The threats to the AI capex boom are real, but the question for investors is whether too much gloom is being priced in, or not enough.The first thing to do is identify the source of the gloom. The problem is neither a lack of demand nor an oversupply of compute. Demand is still outpacing supply, as evidenced by rising GPU rental prices. On a recent Odd Lots episode, Stanley Lee, chief product officer at Liquid Compute, pointed out that rising GPU spot prices may not be as bullish as they seem, as they partly reflect tighter financial conditions in the sector. As capital has become costlier and harder to come by, data center operators have begun requiring bigger upfront payments from customers to secure compute under long-term contracts. As customers also face tighter financial conditions, some of the weaker ones have been forced to buy compute on the spot market, pushing up prices.
